tools.name: build_structure
tools.description: Place a new building. A worker is pulled to build it -- except a trebuchet (trebuchet, trebuchet_advanced): your nearest free engineer builds that, from any distance: one in a formation leaves it and returns to its place after, and the finished trebuchet joins that formation; one on no order stays by the trebuchet. An enemy tower in reach destroys the site; destroyed before its engineer begins, its cost is returned. Given at your own unfinished trebuchet, it sends one more engineer there and places and pays nothing.

tools.name: move_units
tools.description: Persistent movement order. Nearby combat interrupts march/guard/patrol; survivors regroup and resume. Scout never initiates combat. Incoming damage overrides all modes: fighters retaliate together, towers first; mobile threats obey chase limits. Regroup and resume afterward. A new order replaces it only for the units it names; "ordersInProgress" lists each order once with its unitIds. A formation slows its main body so priests and stragglers can rejoin. With a trebuchet, on any move but a scout (guard and hold until they reach their post), an enemy tower known or in sight that comes within the reach of a trebuchet on the way is besieged first (ordersInProgress shows "besieging"), then the order goes on.

mode.description: Default march. Scout: travel without initiating combat; retaliate if attacked. Guard: travel then defend the position, chasing up to 64; there it also goes after whatever damages your units or buildings within 60 of it, trebuchets included, and returns. Hold: travel, then each unit keeps its spot: it attacks only what is within its own reach, and answers whatever attacks it or anything of yours only within 19 of its spot; melee units will not run down archers, so hold under your towers. Patrol: repeat between current group position and destination. New orders replace old ones for selected units.

targets.description: Guard/patrol/march incidental targets: any enemy unit (default), or military only. Pursuit is bounded; explicit attack_target remains a commitment.

targetX.description: Map X. Always together with targetZ.

targetZ.description: Map Z. Always together with targetX.

tile.description: Tile label from map.exploration, e.g. "C5". Used only when targetX/targetZ are not given: the units go to the centre of that tile.

units.description: Object of {"type": count}, e.g. {"champion":3}, or a category like {"infantry":5} (categories only here, never in train_unit). Never an array. Omit for the whole army, trebuchets included; workers are left out: name them to take them. move_units takes {"worker":N} to put a villager on an exact spot; attack_target never takes workers.

unitIds.description: An array of unit ids from friendlyUnits, e.g. [183, 12]: exactly those units and nothing else; wins over "units". Ids are never reused, so a missing one died. Use it when WHICH unit matters: "units" takes whichever are nearest the target.

matchSpeed.description: Optional. "slowestUnit" holds the whole group to its slowest member so they arrive together instead of strung out. Omit to let every unit run at its own speed, which is faster for the quick ones and arrives piecemeal.

formation.description: Optional shape for the MARCH. Every shape keeps the shooters out of the contact rank and the cavalry on the wings. "line" — two ranks of melee, shooters behind, the widest front. "wedge" — a filled triangle, melee at the point. "block" — four to five deep, melee across the front, shooters on both flanks behind it. "screen" — melee ranks, an empty rank, then the shooters. Reforms after combat; reassigned units leave the group. Implies matchSpeed "slowestUnit".

tools.name: attack_target
tools.description: Attack a unit or building by id, or attack-move to a position. Coordinates start a march; "ordersInProgress" in the state carries its secondsRemaining. On a tower, an order that includes a trebuchet stands the army at the trebuchet, out of the tower's reach, until the trebuchet falls; then the army attacks the tower. With a trebuchet along, a known enemy tower covering the point, or coming within the reach of a trebuchet on the way (also on the way to besiege another tower), is besieged so first, and the order goes on once it falls.

targetId.description: Copy the exact string id from enemyBuildings or from an enemyUnits entry with "visible": true, including the unit_ or building_ prefix and full suffix. Do not shorten it or convert it to a number. Use this OR targetX/targetZ.
